title: First hearing Louis Armstrong, Johnny Dunn and the long horns
summary: He first knew Louis from records behind blues singers; they discuss Johnny Dunn's double-time playing and a long trumpet-like horn he cannot name.

story.theme_name: Working with and around Louis Armstrong
story.community_name: Playing with and around Louis Armstrong

blocks.x: Star Trek is pretty good sometimes. You mentioned Louis. When did you first become aware of him?
Oh, way back. He used to play behind a lot of those blues things you know.
(inaudible).
Yeah.
I guess I never (inaudible). There was another trumpet player back in those days too. Smith. And there was one before Louis named Johnnie Duff.

Uh-huh. Who I liked very much at the time. He used to do the double up time thing -- did you know that (inaudible). He used to do it with three majors and then double up the fourth one (singing). And it would like every fourth chord he would do double time you know.
Uh-huh.
Only the notes (inaudible) solo.
Yeah, he did make a lot of records. He did things with the mutes (inaudible).
Yeah, he used to play a lot of those (inaudible) what did they call them?
What did they call them? Randy King and all those trumpet -- , I can't think
of the name of the song. This second Chuck -- this standin for Chuck -- He must have had a long (inaudible).
One of those long taker fellows.
Yeah. I forget what they call them. But it has valves and everything?
Yeah. Well they didn't used to have -- way back in the days where they used to draw the pictures of the angels and things blowing them horns and --
Well it's bugles isn't it?
No, that's not a bugle. This is a long horn -- very long horn. I can't think of the name of it. It has a long --
Did you see him -- Johnnie Dunn?
I didn't see him -- I seen him on the stage -- I didn't know him.
Uhm.
I got to find out what's happening there -- he must have been drugged -- I know he was -- (inaudible). See that? It looks ridiculous don't it?
I don't know -- it's very windy outside. That's probably why it's there. That's what it is -- the wind -- you can hear the wind.
Oh, that's nice. That wind was something else last night.
Uh-huh. Yeah, he went to Europe
Johnnie Dunn?
Yeah.
